clue.text: Blemish found in second-rate auction item

parts.note: B is the grade below A, so second-rate
a lot is an item put up for sale at an auction

explanation.surface: A flaw is spotted in a shoddy piece bought at a sale.
explanation.definitionFit: A blot is a stain or mark that spoils something, a synonym of blemish.

clue.text: Divine creature depicted by male artist

parts.note: he is the male pronoun
RA, Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist

explanation.surface: A heavenly being is painted by a man who is an artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Hera was a goddess, queen of the Greek gods, so a divine being.

clue.text: Criminal tendency

explanation.definitionFit: Corrupt villains are called bent in slang, and a natural inclination is a bent.

clue.text: Can put up the price for fertiliser

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting a word up means writing it from bottom to top

parts.note: a can is a tin
a rate is a charge or price

explanation.surface: A shop is able to raise what it charges for garden fertiliser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' looks like a verb but is the noun TIN, which 'put up' turns into NIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitrates are salts of nitric acid widely spread on fields as nitrogen fertiliser.

clue.text: What numerous readers buy from the leading retailer

definitions.meaning: a book that very many people purchase
read literally, the shop or salesperson that sells most

explanation.definitionFit: A hugely popular book is a best seller, and literally the top vendor is the best seller.

clue.text: Deep despondency of legal drudge in the Royal Horse Guards

indicators.note: the drudge is placed inside the regiment's nickname

parts.note: the Royal Horse Guards were nicknamed the Blues
a devil is a junior barrister doing work for a senior one

explanation.surface: A junior lawyer serving in a cavalry regiment is deeply depressed.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage a barrister's devil does the groundwork for a more senior counsel; the Royal Horse Guards are a British cavalry regiment.
explanation.definitionFit: The blue devils is an old idiom for melancholy or low spirits.

clue.text: Lack of work in the lean years

parts.note: spare can mean thin or lean
time can mean a period of years, an age

explanation.surface: Unemployment is rife during the hungry years.
explanation.definitionFit: Leisure hours free from one's job are spare time, a period without work.

clue.text: Proper way to maintain friendly contact

definitions.meaning: an old adjective meaning fitting or suitable
to get together with someone keeps up a friendship

explanation.definitionFit: Meet is an archaic word for fitting, and getting together keeps friends in touch.

clue.text: An incorrigible beggar!

parts.note: split the word for a beggar into four words and it becomes the cry of someone unable to reform himself

explanation.definitionFit: A mendicant is one who lives by begging, and split up it reads as a confession of being past correcting.

clue.text: Disturb traitor at an Italian restaurant

indicators.note: to disturb the words is to jumble their letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A turncoat is upset while dining at an Italian eatery.
explanation.definitionFit: A trattoria is a simple, informal Italian eating house.

clue.text: Tip rubbish over the hill

indicators.note: to tip something over is to upend it, so the word is turned round
completes the sense of upending the word for nonsense

parts.note: rot is nonsense, rubbish

explanation.surface: Dumping waste over the brow of a hill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tip' suggests a rubbish dump, but 'Tip ... over' signals turning ROT round. A tor is a rocky hill, common on Dartmoor in England.
explanation.definitionFit: A tor is a rocky peak or high hill.

clue.text: Detect that the subtonic has been omitted

parts.note: if something is omitted there is no such thing
te is the seventh ... of the sol-fa scale, the subtonic

explanation.surface: A musician spots that one note of the scale has been left out.
explanation.walkthrough: In tonic sol-fa (do, re, mi, fa, so, la, te) the subtonic is TE; the clue reads 'no te'.
explanation.definitionFit: To note something is to notice or observe it.

clue.text: Perch taken up by the angler

definitions.meaning: a perch is an old unit of length, also called a pole
what a fisherman picks up to fish with

explanation.definitionFit: Rod, pole and perch are the same old measure of length, and an angler fishes with a rod.

clue.text: Sweet English queen

definitions.meaning: a pudding of fruit in a casing of bread or sponge
the wife of George III, a queen consort

explanation.definitionFit: A charlotte is a moulded dessert, and Queen Charlotte was George III's consort.

clue.text: He begrudges paying reduced fee at the ice-rink

parts.note: something at a lowered charge is cheap
what one does at an ice-rink is skate

explanation.surface: A miser will only pay the discounted rate at the skating rink.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheapskate is a stingy person who hates spending money.

clue.text: It prompts the player to cover one storage tank

indicators.note: the performer goes round the other pieces, covering them

parts.note: a player in a theatre is an actor
I is the Roman numeral one
a vat is a large tank for holding liquid

explanation.surface: Something urges a performer to put a lid on a single tank.
explanation.definitionFit: An activator is something that triggers or sets off a process, which is to prompt it.

clue.text: They rent out real estate in the aristocracy

parts.note: land is property in the form of ground
the Lords, as in the House of Lords, are the peerage

explanation.surface: Noble families let out property they own.
explanation.definitionFit: Landlords are owners who let property to tenants.

clue.text: I meet retired clergyman in Buckinghamshire

indicators.note: something retired has withdrawn or gone back, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: Rev is short for Reverend, a clergyman

explanation.surface: I bump into a retired vicar in the Home Counties.
explanation.walkthrough: Iver is a village in Buckinghamshire, an English county west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Iver is a village located in that county, so the phrase points to a place there.

clue.text: Whipping the opposition!

parts.note: both a thrashing with a whip and a trouncing of rivals

explanation.definitionFit: A beating is a flogging, and defeating opponents is also called beating them.

clue.text: Motoring club within eight furlongs-a rare phenomenon

indicators.note: the club goes inside the distance

parts.note: eight furlongs make one mile
the RAC is the Royal Automobile Club, a British motoring organisation

explanation.surface: A motoring club operates within a mile, which is a rare thing.
explanation.definitionFit: A miracle is an extraordinary event that seldom if ever happens.

clue.text: Hazard facing workers of mine

parts.note: a danger to miners is a collapse in the colliery, while the whole is also a general trap

explanation.definitionFit: A pitfall is a hidden danger or trap, and literally a fall of rock in a pit.

clue.text: Black marketeer gets big guns sent back

indicators.note: sending a word back means reading it from right to left

parts.note: big guns are very important people, VIPs

explanation.surface: An illegal trader is given heavy weapons that are returned.
explanation.walkthrough: A spiv is British slang, especially of the 1940s, for a flashy dealer in black-market goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A spiv is a petty crook trading in illicit or rationed goods.

clue.text: Robert Dudley puts Mr Piggott in cooler

indicators.note: the cooler sits inside the jockey's first name

parts.note: Lester Piggott was a famous English jockey
ice cools things

explanation.surface: An Elizabethan nobleman locks a jockey in prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooler' looks like slang for jail, but it is ICE. Robert Dudley was Elizabeth I's favourite, made Earl of Leicester.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Dudley held the title Earl of Leicester, so he was known by that name.

clue.text: Add up half the days between June 21 and September 20

indicators.note: only the first half of the season's name is kept

parts.words: the days between June 21 and September 20
parts.note: that span of dates is summer in the northern hemisphere

explanation.surface: Count up half the days of the season.
explanation.definitionFit: To sum is to total figures, to add them up.

clue.text: A party in trouble

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: A celebration that runs into difficulties.
explanation.definitionFit: Ado means fuss or bother, trouble taken over something.

clue.text: Humorous sketch Saint Christopher

parts.note: Kit is a short form of the name Christopher

explanation.surface: A comic sketch about the patron saint of travellers.
explanation.definitionFit: A skit is a short comic sketch or parody.

clue.text: He advocates change for the Scripture class first

parts.note: RE, religious education, is the school subject of Scripture
a form is a school class
1st, with the one written as I, is first

explanation.surface: A progressive argues that the Bible lesson should come first.
explanation.walkthrough: In British schools a form is a class and RE is religious education. 'first' gives 1ST, read as IST.
explanation.definitionFit: A reformist is someone who campaigns for gradual improvement, a supporter of reform.

clue.text: They throw light on fish

definitions.meaning: flat cartilaginous fish such as skates

explanation.definitionFit: Rays are beams of light, and rays are also flat-bodied fish.

clue.text: I vote against acquiring religious painting

parts.note: a con is an argument or vote against, as in pros and cons

explanation.surface: I oppose buying a sacred picture.
explanation.definitionFit: An icon is a devotional image of a saint, especially in Orthodox churches.

clue.text: Sound value from Eton

indicators.note: the letters are taken from the school's name and made into something new

explanation.surface: The worth of a sound education at Eton.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton is an English public school.
explanation.definitionFit: Tone is the quality or pitch of a musical sound.

clue.text: Wake up in the clink

definitions.meaning: to rouse or begin moving after sleep
the clink is slang for prison

explanation.definitionFit: To stir is to rouse from sleep, and stir is slang for jail.

clue.text: Absurd observation on a fielder's position

parts.note: silly means foolish or absurd
a point is a remark or observation

explanation.surface: A ridiculous remark about where a player stands on the field.
explanation.walkthrough: Silly point is a cricket fielding position very close to the batsman on the off side.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, silly point is a close catching position.
